subject: math
title: Quadrilateral
summary: A quadrilateral is any closed shape with four straight sides and four angles adding to 360°. Explore the family: squares, rectangles, rhombuses, trapezoids, and parallelograms.

crossReferences.label: Triangle (Geometry)
crossReferences.note: A quadrilateral splits into two triangles along a diagonal — that is why its angles sum to 360°.

crossReferences.label: Perimeter (Geometry)
crossReferences.note: The perimeter of a quadrilateral is the sum of its four sides.

crossReferences.label: Area (Geometry)
crossReferences.note: Rectangle area (length × width) is the base formula for area.

compareCandidate.label: Square vs. rhombus
compareCandidate.description: Both have four equal sides, but a square's corners are all right angles while a rhombus can lean — the angles decide.

plainLanguageExplanation: A quadrilateral is any closed shape with four straight sides and four vertices. Its four interior angles always add up to 360°. The family has famous members: a square (four equal sides, four right angles), a rectangle (opposite sides equal, four right angles), a rhombus (four equal sides, leaning angles), a parallelogram (two pairs of parallel sides), and a trapezoid (at least one pair of parallel sides). Unlike a triangle, a quadrilateral is not rigid — a square frame can flex into a rhombus when pushed, which is why gates are braced with a diagonal.

keyFacts.label: Not rigid
keyFacts.value: A square frame flexes into a rhombus

whyItMatters: Quadrilaterals are the shapes of doors, windows, screens, and rooms — the everyday polygons. Knowing their family and the 360° rule lets you measure and build everything rectangular in the real world.
didYouKnow: 'Quadrilateral' comes from Latin — 'quad' (four) and 'latus' (side). That is why a four-sided figure is a 'quad' in so many words: quad bike, quadruple, quadrilateral.
compareReason: Students think all closed shapes are rigid — comparing the flexing quadrilateral with the rigid triangle shows why triangles are used to brace.
